title: Patient satisfaction with different methods of analgosedation for dressing changes in burn patients
summary:
Severe pain can occur during the dressing changes necessary to treat burn injuries, so analgesic sedation with the administration of highly potent painkillers and sleep-inducing medication is carried out. Analgesic sedation refers to the elimination of pain (analgesia) with medication and simultaneous calming (sedation). The aim is to enable the dressing change to be carried out stress-free and pain-free. 
In principle, all medications approved for this indication in anesthesiology can be used. There is currently no preference for any particular procedure or medication. However, this topic is of great clinical importance precisely because of the dressing changes that have to be carried out repeatedly during the course of treatment.  In a clinical study, we would like to compare two established methods of analgesic sedation that are used in clinical routine, including in the burn center, with regard to patient satisfaction with the procedure and also with regard to possible further effects (including saving on pain medication during the course of treatment).
conditions: Burn of unspecified body region, unspecified degree

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
burn injury > 3 % und < 20 % total body surface area (TBSA)
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of consent to participate in the study
Inpatient admission > 24 hours after burn injury
pregnancy
Primarily palliative therapy
Chronic neuropathic pain syndrome
Contraindications to any of the medications used for analgesic sedation
